title: At the table
subtitle: Serving and pairing Touriga Nacional
objectives: Pair dry Touriga Nacional with food

steps.title: Dry wines
steps.body: Dry Touriga Nacional suits roast lamb, kid, game and Portuguese dishes like roast suckling pig from Bairrada or bacalhau with roasted potatoes. Its floral notes go well with herbs and its tannins with fat. Serve at 16 to 18 degrees, decanted when young.

steps.title: Port
steps.body: Ruby and Vintage Ports suit dark chocolate, blue cheese like Stilton, and dried fruit. Serve Port slightly cool, about 16 degrees for ruby and vintage. Vintage Port needs decanting for sediment. Touriga Nacional's structure helps top Vintage Ports age 30 to 50 years.

steps.prompt: Which is a classic partner for Vintage Port?
steps.explanation: Salty blue cheese balances Port's sweetness and power.

steps.title: Ageing
steps.body: Good dry Touriga Nacional from the Douro or Dão ages 10 to 20 years, gaining earthy, savoury notes while keeping its floral lift. Simpler versions are best young and fruity. Port's age depends on style: rubies are best young; vintages last decades.

steps.explanation: Yes. It ages in bottle and throws a heavy sediment.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Touriga Nacional suits lamb, kid and roast pork
Port suits blue cheese and dark chocolate
Good dry reds age 10 to 20 years; Vintage Port decades
